Praying To Quash The Impugned Order

DATED 3.5.2024 PASSED BY THE CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC AT SEDAM IN P.C.R.NO.5/2024 AND REGISTRATION OF THE CASE BY THE RESPONDENT NO.1 IN CRIME NO.10/2024 AGAINST THE PETITIONERS FOR THE OFFENCE PUNISHABLE UNDER SECTIONS 352, 420, 447, 379, 390 AND 34 OF IPC.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY  ORAL ORDER (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY)
1.

Petitioners are before this Court under Section 482 Cr.PC with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in Crime No.10/2024 registered by Kurakunta Police Station, Kalaburagi District, for the offences punishable under Sections 352, 420, 447, 379, 390 read with 34 IPC, arising out of PCR.No.5/2024 pending before the Court of Civil Judge & JMFC, Sedam.
Heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned HCGP for respondent no.1.
Respondent no.2 who is served in the matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29146001/
2 3.

entities.text: N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent no.2 had filed a private complaint in PCR.No.5/2024 before the Court of Civil Judge & JMFC, Sedam, against the petitioners herein, which was referred to the police by the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 156(3) Cr.PC.

entities.text: Court of Civil Judge & JMFC, Sedam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Kurakunta police, inturn have registered FIR in Crime No.10/2024 for the aforesaid offences against the petitioners herein based on such reference order passed in PCR.No.5/2024.
Being aggrieved by the same, the petitioners are before this Court.
4. Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature.
There are civil disputes pending before the Civil Court touching the rights of the parties.

There is no compliance of Section 154(1) & (3) of Cr.PC in the present case, and the complainant has not filed the affidavit along with the private complaint which is the requirement of law as observed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 in the case of MRS. PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA & ANOTHER VS STATE OF U.P. & OTHERS - AIR 2015 SC 1758.

entities.text: MRS. PRIYANKA SRIVASTAVA & ANOTHER VS STATE OF U.P. & OTHERS - AIR 2015 SC 1758
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that investigation of the case is under progress and prima facie case for the alleged offences is made out against the accused.

Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Perusal of the material on record would go to show that the company known as M/s. PSN Medicare Pvt. Ltd., is the successful bidder in the auction that was held by Cement Corporation of India for the purpose of dismantling their cement plant at Karakunta, Sedam Taluk, and rights were granted to the aforesaid company to dismantle the plant.
It appears that petitioner nos.1 & 2 are the Directors of M/s. PSN Medicare Pvt. Ltd., and petitioner no.3 is their employee.

M/ s. PSN Medicare Pvt. Ltd., had executed an agreement in favour of Murali Krishna for dismantling the cement plant and arranging for sale of dismantled material, and inturn Murali Krishna appears to have executed an agreement in favour of the complainant/respondent no.2.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 7.

In the private complaint that is filed on 02.05.2024, it stated that accused nos.1 & 2 along with their men including accused no.3 had entered the cement plant on 02.02.2024 where the defacto complainant was carrying on work of dismantling the plant and by using criminal force, an attempt was made to lift the scrap material which was dismantled and kept inside the plant and when the said attempt was opposed, the accused persons allegedly gave threat to the defacto complainant and it is in this background, the defacto complainant had filed the private complaint.
8.

Perusal of the averments made in the private complaint dated 02.05.2024 would go to show that a statement is made by the defacto complainant that he had approached Kurakunta Police Station immediately after the alleged incident that had taken place on 07.02.2024 and since the PSI was not available in the Station, he had therefore approached the CPI, Sedam, but they had refused to receive his complaint, and thereafter, he had gone to the Superintendent of Police and Inspector General of Police, Kalaburagi, and when even they had refused NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 to receive his complaint, he was constrained to file the private complaint.
N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29146001/
3 9.

entities.text: N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Though such an averment is made in the private complaint, there is no material produced along with the private complaint to show that the defacto complainant had approached the police station,
and thereafter, the higher officers as stated in his private complaint.

A reading of Section 154(3) of Cr.PC would make it very clear that if the police officer incharge of the police station has refused to receive the first information from the aggrieved party, the aggrieved party may forward the information in writing to the higher officers through post.
Such an exercise appears to have not been made in the present case, which would prima facie go to show that there is no compliance of Section 154(1) & (3) of Cr.PC in the present case.
10. Learned Counsel for the petitioners has brought to the notice of this Court that private complaint is not accompanied with an affidavit of the defacto complainant.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Priyanka Srivastava's case supra, in paragraph 27, has observed as under:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 "27.

In our considered opinion, a stage has come in this country where Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.
applications are to be supported by an affidavit duly sworn by the applicant who seeks the invocation of the jurisdiction of the Magistrate.
That apart, in an appropriate case, the learned Magistrate would be well advised to verify the truth and also can verify the veracity of the allegations.
This affidavit can make the applicant more responsible.
We are compelled to say so as such kind of applications are being filed in a routine manner without taking any responsibility whatsoever only to harass certain persons.

That apart, it becomes more disturbing and alarming when one tries to pick up people who are passing orders under a statutory provision which can be challenged under the framework of said Act or under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
But it cannot be done to take undue advantage in a criminal court as if somebody is determined to settle the scores.

We have already indicated that there has to be prior applications under Section 154(1)
and 154(3) while filing a petition under Section 156(3).
Both the aspects should be clearly spelt out in the application and necessary documents to that effect shall be filed.

The warrant for giving a direction that an the application under Section 156(3) be supported by an affidavit so that the person making the application should be conscious and also endeavour to see that no false affidavit is made.
It is because once an affidavit is found to be false, he will be liable for prosecution in accordance with law.
This will deter him to casually invoke the authority of the Magistrate under Section NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 156(3).
That apart, we have already stated that the veracity of the same can also be verified by the learned Magistrate, regard being had to the nature of allegations of the case.

We are compelled to say so as a number of cases pertaining to fiscal sphere, matrimonial dispute/family disputes, commercial offences, medical negligence cases, corruption cases and the cases where there is abnormal delay/laches in initiating criminal prosecution, as are illustrated in Lalita Kumari are being filed.
That apart, the learned Magistrate would also be aware of the delay in lodging of the FIR."
11. Since there is no compliance of the said requirement, the learned Magistrate could not have referred the private complaint to the police under Section 156(3) of Cr.PC.

N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29146001/
4 12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In addition to the same, the material on record would go to show that prior to the defacto complainant approaching the jurisdictional Magistrate by filing a private complaint, he has already filed O.S.No.42/2024 before the jurisdictional Civil Court and it is brought to the notice of this Court that though a prayer for granting temporary injunction was made by him, the same was not granted and only emergent notice was issued on the application filed seeking temporary injunction,
and thereafter, the defacto complainant had filed the private complaint.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 13.

In the plaint in O.S.No.42/2024, a specific mention is made, that on 07.02.2024, the accused persons had entered the premises of the cement plant and tried to stop work of dismantle and tried to lift the scrap by giving threat to the defacto complainant.
However, no mention has been made about the attempt made by the defacto complainant in approaching the police immediately after the alleged incident.

It is for the first time such an averment is made in the private complaint that is filed subsequent to the filing of O.S.No.42/2024.
14.
For the aforesaid reasons, continuation of the impugned criminal proceedings against the petitioners would amount to abuse of the process of law.
Under the circumstances, it is necessary to quash the impugned criminal proceedings.

Accordingly, the following order:
15.
Petition is allowed.

The entire proceedings in Crime No.10/2024 registered by Kurakunta Police Station, Kalaburagi District, for the offences punishable under Sections 352, 420, 447, 379, 390 read with 34 IPC, arising out of PCR.No.5/2024 - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:924 pending before the Court of Civil Judge & JMFC, Sedam, is hereby quashed.

Sd/-
(S.VISHWAJITH SHETTY) JUDGE KK N Kasthur Reddy And Ors vs The State Through And Anr on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29146001/
